schemaAuthority.validationBasis: JSON parse plus structural and cross-reference checks; no repo-local JSON Schema file exists for this format.

assessment.summary: The evidence supports one structural hardening opportunity: make the deliberate import-execution boundary a first-class control so the authoring checker and future runtime preflight do not drift.

nonNegotiables: Preserve ADR-0001 direct per-file method-surface authentication unless explicitly revisited.
Do not treat test-only harness code as authenticated production input.
Preserve canonical in-place and Claude symlink delivery paths.
assumptions: No measured startup latency or memory budget was supplied.
The current Gate-2 branch remains local-only until JP authorizes merge or push.
Runtime pre-import census has not yet been implemented.

evidence.title: User-supplied closure summary
evidence.claim: Reports that the zipimport bypass and disguised-zip bypass were verified, repaired on commit 288e4ca, and rechecked with tests, mutation sweep, dual-path checker runs, adversarial probes, formatting checks, and production identity comparison.

evidence.title: Branch handoff for zipimport closure
evidence.claim: Records the branch state, clean re-review claim, exact changed files, residual risks, and decision to leave the branch unmerged and unpushed.

evidence.title: ADR-0001 module authentication boundary
evidence.claim: Defines the direct per-file authentication decision, Gate 2, runtime pre-import census, fresh cache-prefix obligations, and accepted residuals.

evidence.title: Gate-2 import-closure checker
evidence.claim: Implements the current non-executing authoring gate with complete scripts census, zip-magic sniff, banned identifier checks, and closure/inventory/on-disk equality.

evidence.title: Gate-2 regression tests
evidence.claim: Covers sourceless bytecode, extension artifacts, __pycache__, symlinks, packages, dynamic import aliases, zip archives, disguised zip archives, and benign false-positive controls.

evidence.title: Gate-1 dual-path layout smoke
evidence.claim: Shows bytecode can silently impersonate source, that a fresh cache prefix is necessary but must be invocation-private, and that interpreter selection can vary by invocation form.

evidence.title: Current method-surface inventory
evidence.claim: Shows the current production validator remains a single Python method surface at contract-data-version 5.

opportunities.title: Own the deliberate import-execution boundary as one explicit control
opportunities.summary: Reduce drift between ADR policy, the test-only authoring checker, and the future runtime pre-import census.
opportunities.diagnosis: The known bypasses were local fixes, but they reveal a broader ownership split: the same loader-boundary invariant must be carried by prose, a test-only checker, future runtime code, cache-prefix setup, and method-surface hashing.

evidence.claim: The authoring checker currently owns a detailed scripts census and identifier policy outside production method surfaces.
The future runtime pre-import census must mirror the Gate-2 layout rules before first-party import.
The range of negative cases is broad enough that hand-copying the policy into runtime code creates meaningful drift risk.

desiredInvariants: Before any first-party production import, runtime execution refuses unexpected loadable artifacts under scripts/.
The authoring checker and runtime preflight enforce the same boundary policy, and drift is mechanically visible before release.
Every production Python file that can execute from scripts/ is directly represented in validation.method-surfaces and platform-hashed before helper execution.
Cache freshness is invocation-private and repo-local bytecode is neither read nor written.

options.title: Finish the duplicated gate/runtime pair
options.summary: Keep the current authoring checker and implement a separate matching runtime preflight in the v6 entrypoint.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The runtime can duplicate the repaired cases, but policy drift remains possible.
The handoff's runtime-census concern can be implemented directly, with the drift risk accepted.
This directly implements the current ADR wording.
The checker remains the authoring control and supplies the pattern for the runtime duplicate.
The regression cases can be duplicated for runtime preflight.
The runtime can add the fresh-prefix and direct-bytecode refusals required by the smoke evidence.
The method-surface inventory still version-gates the v6 extraction.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known runtime artifact classes can be refused, but duplicate policy implementations can diverge.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run matching negative cases against authoring checker and runtime preflight.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds one filesystem census before helper import, with no process hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure helper startup time before and after runtime preflight.

tradeoffs.assessment: Uses bounded path sets and a temp cache prefix.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak RSS for representative helper invocations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fail-closed refusals improve safety, but duplicate code creates drift-related false positives or false negatives.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject each forbidden artifact and confirm deterministic refusal before first-party import.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new service or launcher appears; errors remain checker/runtime refusals.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review refusal messages for clear artifact paths and causes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Smallest migration path and easiest rollback.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Revert runtime preflight while preserving current Gate-2 checker if needed.

residualRisks: Policy drift between checker and runtime preflight.
Accepted reflection and external sys.path residuals remain.

acceptanceCriteria: Seeded sourceless .pyc refuses before first-party import.
Disguised zip archive refuses before first-party import.
No repo-local bytecode is created or read.
migrationNotes: Preserve existing Gate-2 checker throughout migration.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert runtime preflight and keep v6 physical extraction blocked.

options.title: Single-source the boundary policy contract
options.summary: Declare the import-boundary policy once and mechanically verify or render both checker and runtime consumers from it.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The bypass classes become policy entries shared by both consumers instead of hand-copied cases.
The handoff's reopened v6 frontier gains a drift-control gate before runtime extraction.
The ADR policy becomes machine-checkable without changing the direct per-file decision.
The checker remains useful but no longer silently owns the only executable policy copy.
Regression cases become coverage for both the policy contract and its consumers.
Cache and interpreter evidence become explicit runtime-policy obligations.
Extends the existing contract-data authority pattern if the policy lives in an authenticated surface; placement must account for method-pin drift or surface-set expansion.

tradeoffs.assessment: Makes policy drift visible and keeps known artifact classes synchronized across authoring and runtime consumers, provided the policy source itself is authenticated or embedded into a pinned runtime surface.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Mutation-test policy-consumer mismatches by removing one forbidden value from either consumer and tamper with any candidate unpinned policy reference to prove runtime cannot consume it directly.

tradeoffs.assessment: Runtime still performs the same census; policy rendering checks run in tests rather than hot path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure helper startup with the runtime preflight using current startup as baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds small policy data and bounded in-memory path sets.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak RSS before and after runtime preflight.

tradeoffs.assessment: Mismatch failures become explicit during validation instead of latent runtime drift.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run structural rendering and mismatch tests in the deliberate validation ladder.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new service appears; operators see refusal errors plus policy mismatch failures during release checks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review error messages for policy version, artifact path, and violated invariant.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds a small policy contract before the v6 cut. If placed in contract-data.yaml it changes an existing pinned surface; if placed in a new pinned file it expands the surface set; if left unpinned it must be edit-time only.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Land policy contract separately or as an explicit pre-v6 gate, classify method-identity consequences, and verify rollback restores the prior method-surface state.

residualRisks: Algorithmic differences can remain even when policy values are shared.
Accepted reflection and external sys.path residuals remain.

workPackages: Choose an authenticated policy placement and record its method-identity consequences.
Bind or compare the checker to the policy.
Bind runtime preflight to the policy without unsafe first-party import.
acceptanceCriteria: The runtime does not read an unpinned policy reference as authority.
Checker and runtime consumers expose the same forbidden artifact and identifier policy.
Removing a policy value from either consumer fails validation.
Runtime refuses seeded artifacts before first-party import through both delivery paths.
migrationNotes: Keep the policy small and declarative to avoid recreating aggregate identity machinery.
Prefer the already pinned contract-data.yaml unless a new pinned file's surface-set expansion is intentionally accepted.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the policy contract and runtime consumer; keep the branch's tactical Gate-2 checker as the blocking guard.

options.title: Run from a launcher-prepared clean module root
options.summary: Stage authenticated source files into an invocation-private clean root before running the validator.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A staged runtime root can make source-tree zip artifacts non-import-visible.
The handoff's runtime-census frontier is handled by a stronger containment boundary.
This may require an ADR amendment because runtime source paths differ from source identity paths.
The checker remains useful as source-tree admission before staging.
The artifact regression set becomes staging rejection coverage.
A clean root and fresh cache reduce ambient bytecode and path-identity hazards, but require new dual-path proof.
The method-surface inventory may need source-to-stage identity rules if runtime paths diverge.

tradeoffs.assessment: Ambient source-tree artifacts are no longer import-visible after staging, but launcher correctness becomes trusted.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prove source-tree artifacts cannot be imported from the staged runtime.

tradeoffs.assessment: Staging can add file copies, path mapping, and startup work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark staged helper startup against current startup and set an acceptance threshold.

tradeoffs.assessment: Invocation roots and staged files add temporary disk and metadata pressure more than heap pressure.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure temp directory size and peak RSS across representative runs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Clean roots improve cleanup isolation but add launcher and mapping failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test partial staging, cleanup failure, interrupted runs, and retry behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators and reviewers must reason about staging diagnostics and source-to-runtime path mapping.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review failure receipts for source path, staged path, and cleanup status.

tradeoffs.assessment: This is the largest compatibility change and likely needs new ADR text.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype in a throwaway branch before binding it to v6.

residualRisks: Source-to-stage identity mapping can complicate capsule evidence.
Accepted external sys.path residuals need redefinition.

acceptanceCriteria: Runtime sys.path cannot reach source-tree artifacts.
Capsule method identity still names authoritative source surfaces.
Interrupted runs clean up staged roots or mark them harmless.
migrationNotes: Do not combine with the first v6 extraction unless recurrence evidence justifies the larger cut.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable launcher staging and return to in-place runtime preflight.

opportunities.recommendation: Use Option 2 under current constraints. It reduces drift between the authoring checker and runtime preflight without changing launch topology during the first v6 extraction, but only if the policy source is authenticated or runtime-consumed values are embedded in a pinned surface.

openQuestions: Decided (JP, 2026-07-16): the already pinned contract-data.yaml owns the policy as a top-level import-boundary section; the other placements are declined. Recorded in the ADR-0001 amendment and proposals/import-execution-boundary.md.

Settled by the implementation plan (2026-07-16), refined by the same-day execution-readiness scrutiny: the entrypoint embeds the census-consumed policy subset, authenticated by the entrypoint's method-surface hash and a non-executing release-time equality test against the contract import-boundary section; _require_boundary_match re-checks it per contract load as post-import defense-in-depth (a pre-import runtime match is circular since the parser is the extracted first-party code, and a pre-import yaml.safe_load read was rejected). Zip detection is structural (zipfile.is_zipfile, two-pass runtime), so there is no zip-magics value. See the ADR-0001 amendment and 2026-07-16 addendum and docs/plans/2026-07-16-deliberate-v6-shared-module-extraction.md.
Should the accepted external sys.path residual remain unchanged after the first module split?
